findings.english_quote: The working text says these people have no repentance; Michigan has “no longer,” Bonner printed p. 108. Alternative: “These no longer have repentance.”
findings.issue: Note b positively attributes “no longer” to Michigan, but the supplied bounded reports do not document that wording at this clause or establish whether its relevant letters are preserved or editorially supplied. Their general report about continuing repentance conditions does not substantiate this particular attribution. The main text faithfully retains the selected negation; the defect is the unsupported certainty of the witness note, not a demonstrated false reading.
findings.suggested_revision: Supply an attributed transcription of the relevant Bonner p. 108 clause, with its brackets and restoration status, before affirming the Michigan reading. Pending that evidence, qualify the note: “The working text says these people have no repentance. A previously attributed Michigan alternative is ‘These no longer have repentance,’ but the supplied comparison does not establish that wording or its preserved versus supplied status.” Retain the selected main-text reading. Any replacement note requires fresh review.

findings.english_quote: The working text says these people have no repentance; Michigan has “no longer,” Bonner printed p. 108. Alternative: “These no longer have repentance.”
findings.issue: Independently assessed against the selected Greek and supplied reports, the simplified edition's note b makes the same unsupported positive attribution of “no longer” to Michigan. The evidence supplied does not quote this reading or distinguish preserved wording from restoration. The simplified main text itself preserves the source's categorical negation.
findings.suggested_revision: Provide a bounded, attributed transcription of the relevant Bonner p. 108 wording and its restoration marks, or disclose the alternative as previously attributed but unverified by the supplied comparison. Do not insert “no longer” into the main text merely because an alternative has been reported. Submit the revised note for fresh review.

summary: Both English texts cover the selected clauses faithfully, including the rod proportions, distinct groups, conditional repentance, categorical negation, and death warnings. The simplified edition was also reviewed directly against the Greek. The version-supported proportion correction is appropriately distinguished from the reported Athos reading, and note d honestly limits the prior “still” attribution. Both editions need a bounded correction to note b's evidentiary certainty. This review evaluates the supplied working source and attributed reports; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify exhaustive collation.
